questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to write a funny advert for a newspaper
Why fewer people now use online dating apps
The language of online dating and its dangers
How psychologists help people after a break-up
questions.why: Sam says they will learn new words used by people looking for love online, and they discuss lies in profiles.

questions.q: Why did people use abbreviations like GSOH in old newspaper dating adverts?
options: They paid per word, so they kept it short
Newspapers did not allow long descriptions of people
They wanted to keep their real identity secret
It was a fashionable way of writing at the time
questions.why: Roy says they paid a price per word, so they described themselves in as few words as possible.

questions.q: What does Roy say happened to the abbreviation GSOH?
options: It was banned from newspapers
It is now only used on dating apps
People stopped using it after the internet came
It became part of everyday English
questions.why: Roy says, 'Eventually, GSOH became a part of everyday English.'

questions.q: According to Dr Nicola Fox Hamilton, when does a dating profile become very deceptive?
options: When someone says they enjoy an activity they do sometimes
When they say they love going out with friends but have none
When someone uses an old photo from many years ago
When someone writes a very short and boring description
questions.why: She says if you have no friends but say your favourite thing is hanging out with friends, that's very deceptive.

questions.q: What does Nicola say many people do in their profiles?
options: Tell the complete truth about their lives
Pretend to be a completely different person
Refuse to say anything about their hobbies
Make things sound a bit better
questions.why: She says a lot of people exaggerate things about themselves to seem more attractive.

questions.q: What balance are people trying to find, according to Nicola?
options: Seeming attractive without disappointing
Being funny without seeming silly or rude
Meeting people online and also in real life
Talking about work and talking about hobbies
questions.why: She says they are balancing 'between being attractive and not completely disappointing'.

questions.q: How is wokefishing different from catfishing, according to Nicola?
options: The person creates a totally false identity
The person is real but lies about their views
The person lies about their job and how much they earn
The person uses someone else's photos and name
questions.why: She says in wokefishing the person is generally who they say, but claims to be more liberal than they are.

questions.q: What does Roy imply with his final advice to listeners?
options: Online dating is too dangerous to try
You should exaggerate a little to find love
It is better to be honest about who you are
Newspaper adverts work better than apps
questions.why: He says 'there's probably someone out there interested in the real you'.
